title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 61
paragraphs: When the Athenians heard this they were eager to come to their help and assist them as much as possible; but as they were already on their way, they were attacked by those Greeks on the king's side who had been ranged opposite them, so that they were no longer able to come to the Lacedaemonians' aid — the force attacking them gave them much trouble. Thus the Lacedaemonians and Tegeans were left alone, numbering together with light-armed men fifty thousand of the former and three thousand Tegeans (the Tegeans were not separated at all from the Lacedaemonians). They began to offer sacrifice, meaning to engage in battle with Mardonius and the force that had come against them. Then, since their offerings did not prove favorable and many of them were being killed in the meantime and many more wounded — for the Persians had made a palisade of their wicker shields and were discharging their arrows in vast numbers and without sparing — Pausanias, seeing the Spartans hard pressed and the offerings not favorable, fixed his gaze on the temple of Plataean Hera and called on the goddess to help, praying that they might by no means be cheated of their hope.
